To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we proposed an energy-quality scalable folded architecture for convolutional neural networks, which is able to adapt to varied per-layer data width and sparse representation, and thus eliminate all computational redundanies by using folding techniques, and achieve high energy efficiency and high area efficiency.

the proposed FPAP architecture can adaptively scale energy efficiency by adjusting the precision of computation, and scale area efficiency by folding convolutional operations into a single FIR filter.
FPAP can achieve energy-quality scalability by folding the MAC operations into adds and the convolution operations into single taps, thus reducing both computational redundancies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy-efficiency and quality tradeoff in CNNs, which is a new trend in hardware architecture for CNNs.
the design of energy-quality scalable architectures for CNNs, which can be used in various emerging applications.
a new hardware architecture for CNNs, which is energy-quality scalable, and has the potential of achieving higher energy efficiency in future CNN applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FPAP is the first energy-quality scalable hardware architecture to support folded precision-adjustable computing for energy-quality scalable CNNs.
FPAP can provide a scalable and flexible hardware platform for CNN applications.
FPAP can achieve the best of both worlds: high efficiency in sparse CNNs and high flexibility for energy-quality scalability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FPAP achieves the best energy-quality scalable performance in sparse CNNs among all existing works.
FPAP achieves the best energy efficiency and area efficiency in the literature.

the folded precision-adjustable architecture, which is able to eliminate computational redundancies in sparse CNNs, can achieve better energy efficiency and area efficiency than the corresponding unfolded design, especially in the case of high sparsity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
folded precision-adjustable processing is an effective way to achieve energy-quality scalability in CNN accelerators.
folding is a promising technique to improve both energy and area efficiency of CNN accelerators.
the folding techniques can be used to eliminate all computational and data redundancies in sparse CNNs, which can lead to significant energy and area savings in hardware implementation of CNNs.
